The directory folded once, for every row of a round

directory_folds.Rd

What the resolution and the check of the Entra account compute from the swept directory alone, whatever the row: the candidates, surnames and given names folded with clean_string(), the contact addresses of every account, the UPNs and the identifiers normalized. A round asked them once per register row, and on a directory of thousands of accounts that was most of the round (measured for the 0.28.0: a quarter of a second for each row, linear in the rows). Computed here they are the same values, from the same functions, once.

Usage

directory_folds(directory)

Arguments

directory

A directory frame as directory_users() returns.

Value

An environment with directory, the directory itself, and rows, candidate, surnames, givens, contacts, contact_values, contact_rows, upns and ids.

Details

Each value is computed the first time it is read, and kept: a promise per field, delayedAssign(). So nothing is computed that the old order did not compute, and in the same order: a row that stops before the directory is looked at reads none of it, and a directory one of these functions refuses (directory_contacts() on columns it cannot line up) stops the round where it stopped it before.

Read only by directory_named(), resolve_against_directory(), entra_account_change() and entra_fill(), each of which takes it as an argument that defaults to folding the directory it is given: a caller that does not pass it gets what it always got. Valid only for the directory it was made from, which is why only provisioning_reconcile() passes one, made from the sweep it hands to the same calls. The directory is kept in the folds, and resolve_against_directory(), entra_account_change() and entra_fill() stop when the one they are handed is not identical() to it: on the same object the comparison ends at the pointers.
